findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime sort keys and crashes on first page
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by='-datetime', so self.key is 'datetime' and get_item_key receives a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime. build_cursor always calls the key callable for non-empty results, so any optimized_pagination=true request from an authorized user fails. value_from_cursor also returns cursor.value as a raw number rather than converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so even if get_item_key were fixed, the generated SQL would compare a datetime column with a numeric value.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets reach Django slicing and produce a 500 response
findings.body: Cursor.from_string and Cursor.__init__ accept arbitrary negative offset values without validation. In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, the advanced branch passes a negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative offsets and will raise ValueError (negative offset is not supported) or produce invalid SQL. An authorized user can trigger this by supplying a crafted cursor such as 0:-1:0 with optimized_pagination=true. The comment claiming the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically is incorrect.

findings.title: No tests cover the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or its advanced negative-offset path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class and a new endpoint code path but includes no tests. This is especially risky because the class is used with a datetime order_by, which its numeric get_item_key cannot handle, and because the negative-offset branch relies on Django behavior that is incorrectly assumed to be safe. Tests for the paginator and the endpoint conditional would have caught both failure modes.
